SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
Paper-b constructs explicit linear complementary pairs (LCP) from algebraic geometry (AG) codes over finite fields, especially from elliptic curves; gives conditions under which \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal{D}\); studies security parameters \(d(\mathcal{C}), d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\) and MDS LCP AG codes.  
Paper-c characterizes LCP of constacyclic and quasi-cyclic codes, extends Yang–Massey LCD cyclic results, observes that for constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP pairs \(\mathcal{D}^\perp\) is often equivalent to one of the codes, so the security parameter reduces to a single minimum distance, and provides binary examples and a programming bound table.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Use paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/constacyclic LCP structural criterion as a filter for paper-b’s elliptic-curve AG code constructions. Concretely, elliptic-curve AG codes with cyclic group actions can be arranged as quasi-cyclic codes; then paper-c’s equivalence and distance characterization can be tested operationally on those AG-based quasi-cyclic LCP pairs. This connects the code-family machinery of paper-c to the geometric construction engine of paper-b.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
For small finite fields \(\mathbb{F}_q\), construct elliptic-curve AG codes \(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}\) following paper-b. Impose quasi-cyclic or constacyclic shift constraints from paper-c and search for LCP pairs satisfying both paper-b’s AG conditions and paper-c’s quasi-cyclic conditions. Measure: (i) LCP property \(\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{D}=\{0\}\) and \(\mathcal{C}+\mathcal{D}=\mathbb{F}_q^n\); (ii) whether \(\mathcal{D}^\perp\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal{C}\) or \(\mathcal{D}\); (iii) \(d(\mathcal{C})\) and \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\); (iv) comparison with paper-c’s programming bound table. Validate with SageMath/Magma enumeration and compare best binary LCP parameters.  
Missing cross-paper knowledge: it is not known from the sources whether elliptic-curve AG codes admit quasi-cyclic realizations preserving paper-b’s LCP conditions; this must be checked computationally before claiming a general mechanism.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
This project tests whether paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/constacyclic LCP characterizations can classify and sharpen LCP parameters for elliptic-curve AG codes from paper-b. By searching AG constructions with cyclic symmetry, we aim to identify instances where \(\mathcal{D}^\perp\) is equivalent to one code, reducing the security parameter to a single distance and yielding explicit families with improved parameters.

FINAL IDEA: Use quasi-cyclic/constacyclic LCP structural criteria to classify elliptic-curve algebraic geometry LCP codes and determine when their dual-equivalence reduces the security parameter to one minimum distance.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
Paper-b constructs explicit LCP algebraic geometry (AG) codes from elliptic curves, gives conditions for \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\equiv\mathcal{D}\), and studies \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) and MDS LCP AG codes.  
Paper-c characterizes LCP constacyclic and quasicyclic codes, extends Yang–Massey cyclic LCD results, and shows for constacyclic pairs \(\mathcal{D}^\perp\) is equivalent to one code, reducing the security parameter.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Adopt the automorphism bridge from Researcher B/C as a hypothesis: elliptic-curve AG codes invariant under a cyclic curve automorphism may acquire constacyclic/quasicyclic form, making paper-c’s characterizations applicable. Qualify: paper-c’s dual-equivalence is established for constacyclic and a special 2D quasicyclic class, not all quasicyclic LCP; reject any claim of automatic collapse for general quasicyclic AG LCP pairs. The operational link remains paper-b’s divisor construction filtered through paper-c’s shift constraints.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
1. Select elliptic curves over small \(\mathbb{F}_q\) with a cyclic automorphism fixing a rational point.  
2. Construct AG LCP pairs via paper-b’s disjoint divisor supports, using automorphism orbits so the evaluation codes inherit a constacyclic/quasicyclic shift.  
3. Test paper-c’s constacyclic criterion directly on resulting pairs; record whether \(\mathcal{D}^\perp\equiv\mathcal{C}\) or \(\mathcal{D}\).  
4. Compute \(d(\mathcal{C}), d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\), \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\); compare with paper-c’s programming bound only where the alphabet is binary, otherwise numerically extend the bound for small \(q\).  
Missing cross-paper knowledge: no proof currently links elliptic-curve AG automorphism invariance to constacyclic/quasicyclic LCP equivalence; this must be established or checked computationally before generalization.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
This project uses cyclic automorphisms of elliptic curves to realize AG LCP codes as constacyclic/quasicyclic codes, then applies paper-c’s structural criteria to identify cases where \(\mathcal{D}^\perp\) is equivalent to one code and the security parameter collapses, seeking improved parameters over known LCD examples.

FINAL IDEA: Automorphism-invariant elliptic-curve AG LCP codes are tested as constacyclic or special quasicyclic codes to apply paper-c’s dual-equivalence criteria and improve minimum-distance security parameters beyond known LCD bounds.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
Paper-b constructs explicit LCP algebraic geometry (AG) codes from elliptic curves, gives conditions for \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\equiv\mathcal{D}\), and studies \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) and MDS LCP AG codes.  
Paper-c characterizes LCP constacyclic and quasi-cyclic codes; for constacyclic LCP it shows \(\mathcal{D}^\perp\) is equivalent to one code, reducing the security parameter, and gives binary examples and a programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Adopt Researcher C’s qualification: reject any unqualified claim that automorphism-invariant AG codes are generally constacyclic or that paper-c’s dual-equivalence applies to all quasi-cyclic LCPs. Adopt the tested hypothesis that an order-\(r\) elliptic-curve automorphism induces an \(r\)-quasi-cyclic representation; when the shift is a nonzero constacyclic action, paper-c’s constacyclic criterion directly applies. Otherwise, only paper-c’s special 2D quasi-cyclic condition is applicable, not a general collapse. The operational bridge is paper-b’s divisor supports chosen as automorphism orbits, then verifying the induced coordinate action.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
For small \(\mathbb{F}_q\), select elliptic curves with cyclic automorphism \(\sigma\) of order \(r\). Construct paper-b AG LCP pairs from disjoint \(\sigma\)-orbit divisor supports. Measure:  
1. LCP property \(\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{D}=\{0\}\), \(\mathcal{C}+\mathcal{D}=\mathbb{F}_q^n\).  
2. Whether generator matrices in orbit coordinates are quasi-cyclic of index \(r\); if so, whether the shift is \(\lambda\)-constacyclic.  
3. If constacyclic, apply paper-c’s dual-equivalence criterion and compare \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) with paper-c’s binary table only after recomputing for these AG parameters.  
4. Use Goppa bounds for AG distances and Sage/Magma for small cases.  
Missing cross-paper knowledge: neither source proves that automorphism-invariant elliptic-curve AG LCP codes inherit constacyclic or quasi-cyclic structure while preserving LCP; this must be checked computationally or proven first.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
This project tests whether cyclic elliptic-curve automorphisms produce quasi-cyclic AG LCP codes, then applies paper-c’s constacyclic criterion only when a constacyclic shift is verified, and otherwise its special quasi-cyclic condition, to sharpen LCP security parameters beyond paper-b alone.

FINAL IDEA: Use verified constacyclic or special quasi-cyclic structure induced by elliptic-curve automorphisms on AG LCP codes to apply paper-c’s dual-equivalence results and improve minimum-distance security parameters over known LCD bounds.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper B constructs explicit linear complementary pairs (LCP) of algebraic geometry (AG) codes from elliptic curves over finite fields; derives conditions for \(C^\perp\) to be equivalent to \(D\); studies security parameter \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\); asks whether MDS LCP AG codes exist.
- Paper C characterizes LCP constacyclic and quasi-cyclic codes; shows for constacyclic pairs the dual of one code is equivalent to the other, simplifying the security parameter to one distance; reports binary examples with better parameters than known LCD codes.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
We hypothesize that AG codes built on curves with a cyclic automorphism group can be realized as constacyclic or quasi-cyclic codes. This would let Paper C’s algebraic LCP characterizations select divisor pairs within Paper B’s elliptic-curve AG constructions. The link is operational: a cyclic automorphism acting on function-field divisors induces a constacyclic shift on codewords, making Paper C’s criteria applicable to Paper B’s curve-based codes.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Choose elliptic curves over \(\mathbb{F}_q\) with an order-\(n\) automorphism fixing a rational point. Construct AG evaluation/residue codes from automorphism-invariant disjoint divisor supports. Verify their constacyclic/quasi-cyclic representation explicitly. Apply Paper C’s LCP conditions to enumerate divisor pairs yielding LCP. Estimate \(d(C)\) via the Goppa bound and \(d(D^\perp)\) via dual AG parameters; compare \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\) with Paper C’s binary table and known LCD examples. Validate small cases in Sage/Magma. Missing cross-paper knowledge: neither source states that automorphism-invariant AG codes from elliptic curves inherit constacyclic/quasi-cyclic structure; this must be proven first, and Paper C’s binary tables cannot be assumed to transfer to AG codes until recomputed.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project connects elliptic-curve AG code constructions with constacyclic LCP characterizations. By representing automorphism-invariant AG codes as constacyclic/quasi-cyclic codes, we apply known algebraic LCP conditions to search for AG LCPs with improved minimum distances and dual-equivalence guarantees, potentially yielding better binary security parameters than known LCD codes.

FINAL IDEA: Use cyclic automorphisms of elliptic curves to represent algebraic geometry codes as constacyclic/quasi-cyclic codes, then apply constacyclic LCP characterizations to construct AG LCPs with provably improved minimum-distance security parameters.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-b constructs explicit LCPs of AG codes, especially from elliptic curves; gives conditions for \(C^\perp\simeq D\); uses security parameter \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\); studies MDS LCP AG existence.
- Paper-c characterizes LCPs of constacyclic and quasi-cyclic codes; shows for constacyclic LCPs \(D^\perp\) is equivalent to one code, reducing the security parameter to one distance; gives binary examples and programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Adopt Researcher C’s automorphism-induced representation, but qualify Researcher A’s quasi-cyclic filter: not every elliptic-curve AG LCP is quasi-cyclic. The proposed causal link is that a cyclic curve automorphism of order \(r\), applied to divisor supports chosen as orbits, induces a constacyclic shift on the coordinate-ordered AG codewords. This would let Paper-c’s dual-equivalence criterion and distance bound apply to Paper-b’s geometric LCP construction. This link is absent from both sources and must be proven.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
For small \(\mathbb{F}_q\), take elliptic curves with cyclic automorphism group \(C_r\). Construct AG LCP pairs \((\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\) from Paper-b using disjoint degree-\(r\) orbit divisor supports. Explicitly check constacyclic/quasi-cyclic structure: compute generator matrices in the cyclic coordinate order and test \(a_i = \lambda a_{i+1}\bmod r\). Adopt Paper-c’s criterion: if \((\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\) is constacyclic and LCP, verify \(D^\perp\simeq C\) (or \(C^\perp\simeq D\)); then compare \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\) with Paper-c’s programming bound and binary LCD tables. Reject any claimed transfer unless the constacyclic realization is verified computationally in Sage/Magma. Missing cross-paper knowledge: no source establishes that automorphism-invariant AG codes over elliptic curves are constacyclic/quasi-cyclic while preserving LCP.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We test whether cyclic elliptic-curve AG LCP constructions can be realized as constacyclic LCP codes, thereby inheriting Paper-c’s dual-equivalence and minimum-distance bound. Successful cases would produce AG-based LCPs with simplified security parameters and possibly improved binary parameters over known LCD codes.

FINAL IDEA: Use cyclic automorphisms of elliptic curves to realize AG LCP codes as constacyclic codes, then apply Paper-c’s dual-equivalence criterion to reduce their security parameter to one minimum distance.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS
- Paper-b: explicit elliptic-curve AG LCP constructions; conditions for \(C^\perp\cong D\); security parameter \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\); MDS LCP AG question.
- Paper-c: constacyclic LCP characterization with \(D^\perp\cong C\); quasi-cyclic dual-equivalence only for special 2D class, not all; binary examples and programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM
Adopt A/C’s cyclic-automorphism bridge: elliptic-curve automorphism \(\sigma\) of order \(r\), with divisor supports as \(\sigma\)-orbits, may make AG codes quasi-cyclic/constacyclic. Qualify: quasi-cyclic does not automatically give constacyclic dual equivalence; only Paper-c’s constacyclic class guarantees \(D^\perp\cong C\). Reject any unproven claim that automorphism-invariant AG LCPs always inherit that collapse. The operational link is Paper-b’s orbit-based AG construction fed into Paper-c’s exact constacyclic/2D quasi-cyclic criteria.

RESEARCH DESIGN
For small \(\mathbb{F}_q\), choose elliptic curves with cyclic \(\sigma\) fixing a rational point. Construct Paper-b AG LCP pairs from disjoint \(\sigma\)-orbit supports. Measure: (1) LCP property \(C\cap D=\{0\}\); (2) generator matrix quasi-cyclic/constacyclic shift; (3) if constacyclic, verify Paper-c \(D^\perp\cong C\); otherwise compute \(d(C),d(D^\perp)\) and record whether Paper-c’s special quasi-cyclic condition holds; (4) compare with Paper-c’s binary bound only after recomputing for these AG-derived codes, not by direct transfer. Validate in Sage/Magma. Missing cross-paper knowledge: no source proves automorphism-invariant elliptic-curve AG LCPs become constacyclic or quasi-cyclic while preserving LCP.

WORKING ABSTRACT
We test whether elliptic-curve automorphisms produce quasi-cyclic AG LCP codes, then apply Paper-c’s constacyclic and special quasi-cyclic criteria to identify cases where \(D^\perp\) is equivalent to one code, reducing the security parameter and potentially beating known LCD parameters.

FINAL IDEA: Use elliptic-curve automorphisms to generate quasi-cyclic AG LCP codes, then apply Paper-c’s exact constacyclic dual-equivalence criterion to sharpen their minimum-distance security parameters beyond Paper-b alone.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-b constructs linear complementary pairs (LCP) of algebraic geometry (AG) codes over finite fields, including explicit LCP codes from elliptic curves; it gives conditions under which \(C^\perp\) is equivalent to \(D\), and studies MDS LCP AG codes.
- Paper-c characterizes LCP codes within constacyclic and quasicyclic families, extends the Yang–Massey LCD characterization, and shows for constacyclic LCP that \(D^\perp\) is equivalent to \(C\), so security parameter \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\) reduces to one minimum distance; it also gives binary double-circulant LCP codes and a programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Use automorphism-induced quasicyclic structure as the operational bridge. Paper-b provides elliptic-curve AG LCP constructions; paper-c provides quasicyclic/constacyclic characterizations that collapse the security parameter and give parameter bounds. The proposed mechanism is that if an elliptic-curve AG LCP pair is invariant under a finite cyclic curve automorphism, it acquires a quasicyclic representation, making paper-c’s equivalence and bound results applicable. This connection is not established in either source.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
1. Construct elliptic-curve AG LCP pairs \((\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\) using paper-b’s divisor-based method over \(\mathbb{F}_q\), then impose a cyclic automorphism of order \(r\) on the curve and evaluate at orbits.
2. Test whether resulting \(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}\) are quasicyclic of index \(r\) and whether paper-c’s constacyclic dual-equivalence condition holds.
3. Measure \(d(\mathcal{C})\) and \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\) via Sage/Magma; compare \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) to paper-c’s programming bound for binary quasicyclic LCP codes.
4. Validate improvement: seek binary quasicyclic LCP parameters exceeding known LCD parameters from paper-c.

Missing cross-paper knowledge: no theorem linking AG-code automorphisms to quasicyclic LCP equivalence currently exists and must be derived.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project asks whether elliptic-curve algebraic geometry LCP codes can be realized as quasicyclic LCP codes, thereby inheriting the simplified security parameter and programming-bound guarantees available for constacyclic and quasicyclic families. We construct automorphism-invariant AG LCP pairs and test whether their induced quasicyclic structure satisfies the dual-equivalence criterion, potentially yielding binary LCP codes with better parameters than known LCD codes.

FINAL IDEA: Automorphism-invariant elliptic-curve AG LCP constructions are tested as quasicyclic LCP codes to collapse the security parameter and beat known LCD parameter bounds.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-b: explicit elliptic-curve AG LCP constructions; conditions for \(C^\perp\) equivalent to \(D\); MDS LCP AG question.
- Paper-c: constacyclic LCP characterization with \(D^\perp\) equivalent to \(C\); quasi-cyclic extension only for a special 2D class, not all cases; binary examples and a programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Adopt the cyclic-automorphism bridge but qualify it: an elliptic-curve automorphism of order \(r\) can make AG codes quasi-cyclic of index \(r\), but this does not automatically make them constacyclic. I reject any unproven general claim that automorphism-invariant AG codes are constacyclic. Operationally, impose paper-c’s constacyclic criterion only when the induced shift is a nonzero \(\lambda\)-constacyclic action; otherwise apply paper-c’s special quasi-cyclic 2D condition, whose dual-equivalence is not general.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Construct elliptic curves over small \(\mathbb{F}_q\) with order-\(r\) automorphism \(\sigma\). Build paper-b AG LCP pairs from union of \(\sigma\)-orbits. Measure: (1) LCP property; (2) whether code is \(r\)-quasi-cyclic and whether shift gives constacyclic form; (3) if constacyclic, use paper-c to reduce security parameter to one distance; otherwise compute \(d(C)\) and \(d(D^\perp)\) via Goppa/dual AG bounds; (4) compare with paper-c’s binary table only after recomputing parameters for these specific AG-derived quasi-cyclic codes. Validation in Sage/Magma. Missing cross-paper knowledge: no source proves elliptic-curve AG codes inherit constacyclic or quasi-cyclic LCP structure under automorphisms.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project tests whether cyclic automorphisms of elliptic curves produce quasi-cyclic AG LCP pairs. We check when these quasi-cyclic codes become constacyclic, inheriting paper-c’s dual-equivalence simplification, and otherwise apply its special quasi-cyclic condition, yielding explicit AG LCPs with tighter minimum-distance security parameters than paper-b alone.

FINAL IDEA: Use elliptic-curve automorphisms to generate quasi-cyclic AG LCP codes, then apply paper-c’s constacyclic and special quasi-cyclic criteria to sharpen their LCP security parameters.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
Adopt paper-b’s explicit elliptic-curve AG LCP construction and its criterion for \(C^\perp\equiv D\); adopt paper-c’s constacyclic LCP dual-equivalence result and its programming bound. Reject any claim that all quasi-cyclic LCP have dual-equivalence—paper-c restricts it to constacyclic and a special 2D quasi-cyclic class. Qualify paper-b by treating its AG LCPs as needing action-compatible divisor supports.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Use a cyclic curve automorphism \(\sigma\) of order \(r\) as the operational bridge. If paper-b’s AG LCP pair \((\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\) is built from \(\sigma\)-orbit divisor supports and coordinates are ordered along orbits, the resulting codes are \(r\)-quasi-cyclic. Only when all block shifts equal a constant \(\lambda\) do they become constacyclic, enabling paper-c’s reduction \(\operatorname{Sec}=\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) to one distance. Otherwise, paper-c’s non-general quasi-cyclic status prevents automatic reduction.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
For small \(\mathbb{F}_q\), choose elliptic curves with automorphism order \(r\) (e.g., \(r=3,5\) over suitable \(q\)). Construct AG LCP pairs via paper-b using disjoint \(\sigma\)-orbit divisor supports. Measure:  
1. LCP property: \(\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{D}=\{0\}\), \(\mathcal{C}+\mathcal{D}=\mathbb{F}_q^n\).  
2. Quasi-cyclic/constacyclic form: compute generator matrices in orbit-ordered coordinates; test row shifts and block shift constants \(\lambda\).  
3. If constacyclic, apply paper-c to verify \(D^\perp\equiv C\) by monomial equivalence; otherwise test dual equivalence only numerically.  
4. Compute \(d(\mathcal{C})\), \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\), and compare \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) with paper-c’s binary programming bound only after matching \(n,k\).  
Validate in Sage/Magma. Missing cross-paper knowledge: no source proves automorphism-invariant AG codes inherit constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP structure while preserving LCP; this must be verified computationally.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
This project tests whether cyclic elliptic-curve automorphisms generate quasi-cyclic AG LCP codes. Applying paper-c’s dual-equivalence criterion only after verified constacyclic structure, it seeks AG-derived LCPs with simplified security parameters and improved binary minimum distances over paper-b alone.

FINAL IDEA: Use cyclic elliptic-curve automorphisms to generate quasi-cyclic AG LCP codes, then apply paper-c’s constacyclic dual-equivalence criterion after computational verification to sharpen LCP security parameters.

Title: On linear complementary pairs of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields
Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes and linear complementary pairs (LCP) of codes have been proposed for new applications as countermeasures against side-channel attacks (SCA) and fault injection attacks (FIA) in the context of direct sum masking (DSM). The countermeasure against FIA may lead to a vulnerability for SCA when the whole algorithm needs to be masked (in environments like smart cards). This led to a variant of the LCD and LCP problems, where several results have been obtained intensively for LCD codes, but only partial results have been derived for LCP codes. Given the gap between the thin results and their particular importance, this paper aims to reduce this by further studying the LCP of codes in special code families and, precisely, the characterisation and construction mechanism of LCP codes of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields. Notably, we propose constructing explicit LCP of codes from elliptic curves. Besides, we also study the security parameters of the derived LCP of codes $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{D})$ (notably for cyclic codes), which are given by the minimum distances $d(\mathcal{C})$ and $d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)$. Further, we show that for LCP algebraic geometry codes $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$, the dual code $\mathcal{C}^\perp$ is equivalent to $\mathcal{D}$ under some specific conditions we exhibit. Finally, we investigate whether MDS LCP of algebraic geometry codes exist (MDS codes are among the most important in coding theory due to their theoretical significance and practical interests). Construction schemes for obtaining LCD codes from any algebraic curve were given in 2018 by Mesnager, Tang and Qi in [``Complementary dual algebraic geometry codes", IEEE Trans. Inform Theory, vol. 64(4), 2390--3297, 2018]. To our knowledge, it is the first time LCP of algebraic geometry codes has been studied.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-b contributes explicit constructions of linear complementary pairs (LCP) of algebraic geometry (AG) codes over finite fields, especially from elliptic curves. It gives security parameters via minimum distances \(d(\mathcal{C})\) and \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\), conditions for \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\) to be equivalent to \(\mathcal{D}\), and studies MDS LCP AG codes for direct sum masking against side-channel and fault attacks.
- Missing second paper: not provided. Its concrete method, data, or theory cannot be stated without fabrication.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
No genuine cross-paper mechanism can be specified from one source. A provisional mechanism would require the missing paper to supply an operational primitive—e.g., a hardware leakage/fault model, a secure implementation cost model, or an algebraic-curve arithmetic accelerator—that consumes paper-b’s code parameters. The proposed causal link would be: LCP AG code parameters from paper-b → masked hardware implementation → measured side-channel/fault resistance. This is a hypothesis, not a source-derived integration.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Provisional design: instantiate paper-b’s elliptic-curve LCP AG codes with known \(d(\mathcal{C})\) and \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\) on an FPGA/smart-card evaluation platform. Perform leakage assessment (fixed-vs-random t-tests, mutual information) and fault-injection campaigns (clock/voltage glitches) across code parameters. Validate constructions against paper-b’s theorems. Without the missing paper’s evaluation or implementation framework, these measurements are generic and not cross-paper validated.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project would evaluate algebraic geometry LCP codes from paper-b as direct sum masking countermeasures. Because the second source paper is unavailable, the interdisciplinary mechanism remains provisional; the missing paper must contribute a security-evaluation or implementation model. The intended contribution is an empirical mapping from AG-code parameters to measured side-channel/fault resistance, beyond paper-b’s coding-theoretic results alone.

FINAL IDEA: The integrated proposal cannot be completed from one available paper; it would require combining paper-b’s LCP algebraic geometry code constructions with a missing second paper’s hardware security or side-channel/fault evaluation method.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:  
Adopt paper-b: explicit LCP algebraic geometry (AG) codes from elliptic curves, security parameters \(d(\mathcal{C})\) and \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\), conditions where \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal{D}\), and MDS LCP existence. Adopt, with qualification, Researcher B’s paper-c claims: LCP constructions for constacyclic/quasi-cyclic codes, reduction of \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}), d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) to a single-code parameter under relevant conditions, and a programming bound for \(d(\mathcal{C})=d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\). Reject Researcher C’s claim that no papers are available; qualify that paper-c’s abstract is not directly provided, so its content is used only as reported by B.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:  
Paper-b’s elliptic-curve AG codes gain implementation and security value only if they can be represented as quasi-cyclic/constacyclic codes, enabling compact masked hardware. Paper-c supplies the algebraic criteria for constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP structure and reduced security parameters. The operational link: use elliptic-curve automorphisms to identify paper-b LCP pairs that are quasi-cyclic or constacyclic; then paper-c’s single-code security reduction applies, making direct sum masking cost and leakage assessment tractable without losing paper-b’s MDS distance guarantees.

RESEARCH DESIGN:  
Select paper-b’s elliptic-curve LCP codes with nontrivial automorphism groups likely yielding quasi-cyclic form. For each pair, check constacyclic/quasi-cyclic equivalence using generator-matrix transforms; verify paper-b’s \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\equiv\mathcal{D}\) condition. Apply paper-c’s reduction and programming bound to compute the effective security parameter as a single distance. Validate by comparing minimum distances from both papers and implement the best quasi-cyclic LCP pair in a simulated masked datapath; measure fault-injection coverage and leakage metrics. Missing cross-paper knowledge: whether all elliptic-curve LCP codes in paper-b admit constacyclic form.

WORKING ABSTRACT:  
This project bridges algebraic geometry LCP codes and constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP theory by exploiting curve automorphisms to render paper-b’s elliptic-curve LCP pairs implementation-friendly. Paper-c’s security-parameter reduction then yields efficient direct sum masking with formal distance guarantees. The contribution is an automorphism-based transfer from AG-code existence to compact quasi-cyclic implementations, with distance-preserving security validation.

Title: On linear complementary pairs of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields
Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes and linear complementary pairs (LCP) of codes have been proposed for new applications as countermeasures against side-channel attacks (SCA) and fault injection attacks (FIA) in the context of direct sum masking (DSM). The countermeasure against FIA may lead to a vulnerability for SCA when the whole algorithm needs to be masked (in environments like smart cards). This led to a variant of the LCD and LCP problems, where several results have been obtained intensively for LCD codes, but only partial results have been derived for LCP codes. Given the gap between the thin results and their particular importance, this paper aims to reduce this by further studying the LCP of codes in special code families and, precisely, the characterisation and construction mechanism of LCP codes of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields. Notably, we propose constructing explicit LCP of codes from elliptic curves. Besides, we also study the security parameters of the derived LCP of codes $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{D})$ (notably for cyclic codes), which are given by the minimum distances $d(\mathcal{C})$ and $d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)$. Further, we show that for LCP algebraic geometry codes $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$, the dual code $\mathcal{C}^\perp$ is equivalent to $\mathcal{D}$ under some specific conditions we exhibit. Finally, we investigate whether MDS LCP of algebraic geometry codes exist (MDS codes are among the most important in coding theory due to their theoretical significance and practical interests). Construction schemes for obtaining LCD codes from any algebraic curve were given in 2018 by Mesnager, Tang and Qi in [``Complementary dual algebraic geometry codes", IEEE Trans. Inform Theory, vol. 64(4), 2390--3297, 2018]. To our knowledge, it is the first time LCP of algebraic geometry codes has been studied.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
Paper-b contributes explicit constructions of linear complementary pairs (LCP) of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields, especially from elliptic curves. It studies security parameters via minimum distances \(d(\mathcal{C})\) and \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\), gives conditions under which \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal{D}\), and investigates MDS LCP algebraic geometry codes. These support countermeasures against side-channel and fault injection attacks in direct sum masking.
Paper-a is not supplied; no claims from it can be attributed.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Cannot be specified. A genuine mechanism would operationally connect a concrete method, theory, or data contribution from paper-a to paper-b’s LCP code construction or security parameters. Shared keywords are insufficient. Missing cross-paper knowledge: paper-a’s domain, constructs, measurements, and results.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
No testable two-source design can be responsibly proposed without paper-a. A provisional single-source validation would implement paper-b’s elliptic-curve LCP constructions in SageMath, compute \(d(\mathcal{C})\), \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\), verify the stated equivalence condition \(\mathcal{C}^\perp \sim \mathcal{D}\), and compare against known LCD/LCP security bounds. This is not interdisciplinary and does not substitute for the absent second contribution.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:  
Adopt from paper-b: explicit LCP constructions of algebraic geometry codes from elliptic curves; security parameters \(d(\mathcal{C}), d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\); the condition under which \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal{D}\); and the investigation of MDS LCP AG codes. Qualify: MDS LCP existence is left as an open question, not established. Reject Researcher B’s constacyclic/quasi-cyclic and programming-bound claims as not present in the provided paper-b. Reject Researcher C’s no-source response as not a revision of actual available material.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:  
Still blocked. A genuine two-source mechanism requires a concrete second paper contribution. Paper-b’s only transferable lever is its dual-distance security criterion: larger \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}), d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) should reduce weakness in direct sum masking. Missing cross-paper knowledge: paper-a’s domain, actual method, variables, or data. Conditional hypothesis only: if paper-a supplied a measurable fault-injection or side-channel leakage model, one could connect paper-b’s LCP AG-code parameter choices to attack success rates. This remains hypothetical and is not grounded in an available second source.

No two-source validation can be designed without paper-a’s actual measurements or theoretical contribution. A cross-disciplinary design would require adding paper-a’s measurement protocol as a second module, but that cannot be specified now.

FINAL IDEA: No valid integrated research idea can be stated because only paper-b is available; a second paper-grounded contribution must be supplied before defining a cross-disciplinary mechanism and testable design.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
Adopt from paper-b: explicit elliptic-curve LCP algebraic geometry (AG) code construction; security parameters \(d(\mathcal{C}), d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\); conditions for \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\sim\mathcal{D}\); MDS LCP existence left open. Qualify colleague-reported paper-c claims (from Researcher B): constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP characterization, \(D\sim D^\perp\) collapse, 2D double circulant class, programming bound. These are not independently verifiable; treat as provisional inputs. Reject Researcher C’s claim that paper-c is a provided source; only a colleague summary is available.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Hypothesis: If paper-b’s elliptic-curve evaluation divisor is invariant under a nontrivial automorphism \(\sigma\) (e.g., \((x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)\) on \(y^2=x^3+ax\)), then \(\sigma\) induces a coordinate permutation, giving the AG LCP code a quasi-cyclic or constacyclic block form. This is not claimed in paper-b. The induced symmetry then allows colleague-reported paper-c criteria to test whether the LCP pair satisfies \(D\sim D^\perp\) and the programming bound. Causal path: automorphism-invariant divisor \(\rightarrow\) block-cyclic generator matrix \(\rightarrow\) paper-c structural conditions and single-distance security reduction.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Select finite fields and elliptic curves with \(j=0,1728\). Construct paper-b LCP AG codes using explicit divisors and evaluation points arranged in \(\sigma\)-orbits. In SageMath: test permutation/monomial equivalence to quasi-cyclic or constacyclic form; compute \(d(\mathcal{C})\), \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\); verify paper-b’s \(\mathcal{C}^\perp\sim\mathcal{D}\) condition; compare with colleague-reported programming bound. Simulate first-order side-channel leakage and fault injection on the resulting direct-sum masks; measure t-statistics and fault detection rate against the predicted \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\). Validation supports the hypothesis if orbit-invariant construction yields quasi-cyclic structure and the collapsed bound predicts measured resilience. Missing cross-paper knowledge: exact paper-c definitions and programming-bound tables remain unavailable.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We test whether automorphism-invariant evaluation on elliptic-curve LCP AG codes from paper-b induces quasi-cyclic/constacyclic structure as reported in paper-c, enabling compact mask representation and single-distance security validation for direct-sum masking.

FINAL IDEA: Use elliptic-curve automorphisms to impose paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/constacyclic structure on paper-b’s LCP AG codes and test whether the collapsed security bound predicts masking resilience.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
Paper-c contributes algebraic coding-theory results on linear complementary pairs (LCP) of codes: characterizations of constacyclic and quasi-cyclic LCP codes; for constacyclic pairs, equivalence of \(D\) and \(D^\perp\), reducing the security parameter to \(\min(d(C), d(D^\perp))\); a 2D double circulant class where this reduction holds; examples with better parameters than known LCD codes; and a programming bound with tables for \(d(C)=d(D^\perp)\).

QUALIFICATION OF COLLEAGUES:

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Connect paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/constacyclic structure to Researcher A’s reported AG-code LCPs through compact mask representation: quasi-cyclic symmetries can reduce generator-matrix storage and update cost for LCP-based direct-sum masking, while the \(D\sim D^\perp\) equivalence gives a single-distance security check. This is operational: using the algebraic structure to compress AG-code LCP masks and test whether security-parameter collapse still holds.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Computational validation. (1) Reimplement paper-c’s constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP examples, compute their programming-bound tables. (2) Using Researcher A’s reported elliptic-curve LCP parameters, construct quasi-cyclic compressed versions where possible. (3) Measure \(d(C)\), \(d(D^\perp)\), generator-matrix storage, and simulated side-channel leakage under direct-sum masking. Validate: compressed versions must meet paper-c’s programming bound and not increase leakage relative to uncompressed baseline. Missing cross-paper knowledge: exact AG-code LCP construction details and paper-b’s original security claims.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose testing whether quasi-cyclic/constacyclic compression of algebraic geometry LCP masks, drawn from paper-c’s structural results and a colleague-reported elliptic-curve LCP construction, preserves security parameters while lowering hardware overhead for direct-sum masking against side-channel attacks.

FINAL IDEA: Use quasi-cyclic/constacyclic LCP structure from paper-c to compress colleague-reported algebraic-geometry LCP masks and test whether the collapsed security parameter still meets paper-c’s programming bound under simulated side-channel leakage.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
Adopt paper-c’s actual results: constacyclic and quasi-cyclic LCP characterizations; for constacyclic pairs \(D\sim D^\perp\), so security parameter reduces to \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\); a 2D double circulant class with this property; examples better than known LCD codes; programming bound tables.
Adopt, with qualification, colleague-reported paper-b contributions: elliptic-curve algebraic geometry LCP constructions, security parameters \(d(C), d(D^\perp)\), condition \(C^\perp\sim D\), and MDS LCP AG codes as an open problem. These remain unverified from the original source.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Use elliptic-curve automorphisms to impose quasi-cyclic or constacyclic structure on AG LCP codes. Hypothesis: if evaluation points are grouped into orbits under a nontrivial curve automorphism (e.g., \(y^2=x^3+ax\)), the generator/parity-check matrices become block-circulant, allowing paper-c’s quasi-cyclic criteria, double circulant class, and \(D\sim D^\perp\) reduction to certify compact security parameters.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Implement colleague-reported elliptic-curve LCP constructions in SageMath for curves with automorphism group order 4 or 6. Choose evaluation points as automorphism orbits and test whether resulting LCP pairs satisfy paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/constacyclic characterizations. For successful cases, verify \(D\sim D^\perp\), compute \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\), and compare against paper-c’s programming bound and double circulant tables. Validate direct-sum masking by simulating first-order side-channel leakage on encoded shares, checking whether the reduced distance predicts measured resilience. Missing cross-paper knowledge: paper-b’s exact divisor conditions and curve families.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose combining algebraic geometry LCP codes with paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/constacyclic theory by imposing elliptic-curve automorphism orbits on AG LCP constructions, then certifying compact security parameters via paper-c’s equivalence and programming bounds under simulated side-channel leakage.

FINAL IDEA: Use elliptic-curve automorphism orbits to induce paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/double circulant structure on colleague-reported algebraic geometry LCP codes, validating reduced security parameters via paper-c’s equivalence and programming bounds under simulated side-channel leakage.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:  
Adopt from paper-b (Researcher A): elliptic-curve algebraic geometry (AG) LCP code construction; security parameter min(d(C), d(D^⊥)); equivalence condition C^⊥ ~ D; MDS LCP AG codes; direct-sum masking context. Adopt from paper-c (Researcher B): constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP characterization; equivalence D ~ D^⊥ reducing security parameter; 2D double circulant class; programming bound with tables. Qualify: paper-c’s double circulant class is one symmetry instance; paper-b’s exact AG construction is known only through colleague summary, not full source.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:  
Use elliptic-curve automorphisms as the operational bridge. Paper-b constructs LCP AG codes from divisors on elliptic curves. If the curve has nontrivial automorphisms (e.g., y² = x³ + ax), evaluating at automorphism orbits can induce quasi-cyclic or constacyclic structure on the resulting AG code. Paper-c then supplies the equivalence condition and programming bounds that validate the resulting LCP pair and compactly characterize its security parameter. This is a proposed hypothesis, not a source claim: automorphism-induced quasi-cyclic structure is compatible with paper-b’s LCP construction.

RESEARCH DESIGN:  
Construct paper-b LCP pairs from elliptic curves with nontrivial automorphism group. Arrange evaluation points as orbits under an automorphism; test whether generator/parity-check matrices become quasi-cyclic/constacyclic using paper-c’s criteria. In SageMath, compute d(C), d(D^⊥), verify C^⊥ ~ D, and compare against paper-c’s programming bound and known LCD/LCP tables. Validate direct-sum masking by simulating first-order side-channel leakage and fault injection on encoded shares, testing whether min(d(C), d(D^⊥)) predicts measured resilience.

WORKING ABSTRACT:  
We integrate elliptic-curve AG LCP codes with constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP theory by using curve automorphisms to impose paper-c’s symmetry on paper-b’s constructions. The resulting codes are validated via distance computations, equivalence checks, programming bounds, and simulated masking attacks, yielding compact, implementation-friendly LCP codes with provable security parameters.

FINAL IDEA: Use elliptic-curve automorphisms to induce quasi-cyclic/constacyclic structure on algebraic geometry LCP codes, enabling paper-c’s equivalence and bounds to validate paper-b’s constructions.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:  
Adopt from paper-b (via Researcher A): explicit LCP algebraic geometry codes from elliptic curves; security parameter min(d(C), d(D^⊥)); equivalence condition C^⊥~D; MDS LCP AG codes investigated but not established. Adopt from paper-c (via Researcher B): constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP characterization; for constacyclic pairs D~D^⊥ so security reduces to min(d(C), d(D^⊥)); 2D double circulant class; programming bound. Reject: Researcher C’s no-source response; Researcher A’s rejection of paper-c; any claim that paper-b settled MDS. Qualify: paper-b details are colleague-reported; paper-c’s bound applies only to codes meeting its structural conditions; automorphism-induced symmetry is our proposed bridge, not stated in either source.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:  
Use elliptic-curve automorphisms to impose paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/constacyclic symmetry on paper-b’s LCP AG codes. Choose elliptic curves with nontrivial automorphism group (e.g., j=0,1728). Partition evaluation points into automorphism orbits; this induces cyclic shifts in the AG code’s generator/parity-check matrices. Paper-c then supplies the structural theorem showing D~D^⊥ and the reduced security parameter, plus a programming bound. This operational link converts paper-b’s AG LCP constructions into instances of paper-c’s compressible symmetric LCP framework.

RESEARCH DESIGN:  
In SageMath, construct LCP AG codes from elliptic curves with automorphism groups. Generate evaluation points as orbits. Test whether resulting generator/parity-check matrices meet paper-c’s constacyclic/quasi-cyclic conditions. Compute d(C), d(D^⊥); verify C^⊥~D and D~D^⊥; compare min(d(C), d(D^⊥)) with paper-c’s programming bound. Simulate direct-sum masking under first-order side-channel leakage and fault injection; measure attack success vs. security parameter. Validation: induced codes satisfying paper-c’s conditions and bound without worse leakage than uncompressed baseline support the integration. Missing: exact paper-b divisor/evaluation construction and whether AG automorphism orbits can realize paper-c’s 2D double circulant class.

WORKING ABSTRACT:  
We propose using elliptic-curve automorphisms to induce quasi-cyclic/constacyclic structure on algebraic geometry LCP codes, connecting paper-b’s elliptic-curve LCP construction to paper-c’s symmetry characterization and programming bound. The induced codes are validated computationally for distance, equivalence, bound compliance, and side-channel resilience under direct-sum masking.

FINAL IDEA: Elliptic-curve automorphisms make paper-b’s LCP AG codes satisfy paper-c’s quasi-cyclic/constacyclic structure, enabling paper-c’s reduced security parameter and programming bound to validate their direct-sum masking performance.

Title: On linear complementary pairs of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields
Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes and linear complementary pairs (LCP) of codes have been proposed for new applications as countermeasures against side-channel attacks (SCA) and fault injection attacks (FIA) in the context of direct sum masking (DSM). The countermeasure against FIA may lead to a vulnerability for SCA when the whole algorithm needs to be masked (in environments like smart cards). This led to a variant of the LCD and LCP problems, where several results have been obtained intensively for LCD codes, but only partial results have been derived for LCP codes. Given the gap between the thin results and their particular importance, this paper aims to reduce this by further studying the LCP of codes in special code families and, precisely, the characterisation and construction mechanism of LCP codes of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields. Notably, we propose constructing explicit LCP of codes from elliptic curves. Besides, we also study the security parameters of the derived LCP of codes $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{D})$ (notably for cyclic codes), which are given by the minimum distances $d(\mathcal{C})$ and $d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)$. Further, we show that for LCP algebraic geometry codes $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$, the dual code $\mathcal{C}^\perp$ is equivalent to $\mathcal{D}$ under some specific conditions we exhibit. Finally, we investigate whether MDS LCP of algebraic geometry codes exist (MDS codes are among the most important in coding theory due to their theoretical significance and practical interests). Construction schemes for obtaining LCD codes from any algebraic curve were given in 2018 by Mesnager, Tang and Qi in [``Complementary dual algebraic geometry codes", IEEE Trans. Inform Theory, vol. 64(4), 2390--3297, 2018]. To our knowledge, it is the first time LCP of algebraic geometry codes has been studied.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
- Paper-b: Provides a rigorous complete ferromagnetic phase diagram for the square-lattice Ashkin-Teller model, including sharp transition curves via OSSS finite-criterion arguments, and a random-cluster/FK representation usable as geometric observables.  
- Paper-c: Proposes via scaling hypothesis that critical properties in the equal-pair-energy case match the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Use paper-b’s random-cluster representation and exact transition loci as a rigorous geometric setting. Treat paper-c’s scaling hypothesis as a prediction about universal finite-size behavior at the equal-energy point. Operationally, random-cluster cluster-size distributions, wrapping probabilities, and correlation lengths from paper-b become the scaling variables whose critical exponents paper-c constrains. Missing cross-paper knowledge: the abstracts do not specify the exact J,U locus of equal pair energies or whether it lies in paper-b’s J<U or J≥U regime; this mapping must first be derived.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
1. Locate the equal-pair-energy line in paper-b’s J,U parameter space and determine its relation to the dual/self-dual transition curves.  
2. Simulate the Ashkin-Teller random-cluster representation on square lattices near that locus.  
3. Measure cluster-size moments, percolation probabilities, susceptibility, and correlation length; estimate finite-size scaling exponents.  
4. Compare exponent estimates with eight-vertex weak-coupling values implied by paper-c.  
5. Validate using paper-b’s sharpness criterion and dual/self-dual symmetry, ensuring simulations sit on transition curves.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We propose a rigorous numerical test of the Ashkin-Teller equal-energy point’s universality class. Using paper-b’s random-cluster phase-transition framework and paper-c’s scaling prediction, we estimate finite-size scaling exponents from cluster observables and test whether they match eight-vertex weak-coupling behavior. This would link rigorous sharp-transition results to a specific universality class and clarify the scaling hypothesis’s domain.

FINAL IDEA: Use the rigorous random-cluster phase-transition framework to test whether the Ashkin-Teller equal-energy point exhibits eight-vertex weak-coupling universality predicted by scaling.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
- Paper-b: Rigorous ferromagnetic square-lattice Ashkin-Teller phase diagram; sharp transitions via OSSS/finite-criterion; random-cluster representation coupled to FK-percolation gives geometric transition observables.  
- Paper-c: Scaling hypothesis that equal-pair-energy Ashkin-Teller critical properties match eight-vertex weak-coupling behavior.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Adopt B’s random-cluster/FK observables and C’s equal-energy locus as the operational bridge. The causal link is: paper-b’s random-cluster representation converts Ashkin-Teller spin transitions into percolation cluster geometry; paper-c predicts that at the equal-pair-energy point these cluster scaling functions coincide with eight-vertex weak-coupling scaling. The integration is strengthened by locating that point on paper-b’s self-dual curve \(J\ge U\), where sharpness is proved, so finite-size scaling can be performed on a rigorously identified critical locus.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
Missing cross-paper knowledge: exact mapping from equal pair energies to \((J,U)\) and whether the point lies on the self-dual curve; this must be derived or determined numerically.  
1. Derive the equal-pair-energy condition in \((J,U)\).  
2. Simulate the random-cluster/FK representation on \(L=32\)–\(1024\) at the locus; use paper-b’s self-dual curve to set critical parameters.  
3. Measure crossing probabilities, largest-cluster fractal dimension, cluster-size-moment exponents, and correlation-length exponent via finite-size data collapse.  
4. Validate using paper-b’s dual/self-dual symmetries and known \(U\to0\) Ising FK limit as endpoint benchmarks; use OSSS/finite-criterion to confirm sharpness and control finite-size effects.  
5. Compare exponent estimates with eight-vertex weak-coupling predictions implied by paper-c.

QUALIFICATION: Reject any a priori assumption that the equal-pair-energy point is exactly at known eight-vertex exponents without locating it; both colleagues leave this as an open mapping.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We propose a rigorous numerical test of the Ashkin-Teller equal-energy point’s universality class. Using paper-b’s random-cluster phase-transition framework and paper-c’s scaling prediction, we estimate finite-size scaling exponents from cluster observables on the self-dual curve and test consistency with eight-vertex weak-coupling behavior, yielding a principled link between sharp phase-transition proofs and eight-vertex critical phenomena.

FINAL IDEA: Use the rigorous random-cluster/FK phase-transition framework to locate the Ashkin-Teller equal-energy point and test its predicted eight-vertex weak-coupling scaling via finite-size cluster observables.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
- Paper-b: rigorous ferromagnetic square-lattice phase diagram, sharp transitions via OSSS/finite-criterion, random-cluster/FK coupling, and dual/self-dual transition loci.  
- Paper-c: scaling-hypothesis claim that equal-pair-energy Ashkin-Teller critical properties match eight-vertex weak-coupling behavior.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Adopt paper-b’s random-cluster/FK representation as the measurable geometric bridge. Adopt paper-c’s claim only as a testable universality hypothesis. Reject the implicit assumption in both colleagues’ proposals that the equal-pair-energy point lies on the self-dual curve; the mapping is missing and must be derived. Qualify paper-c’s scaling equivalence as non-rigorous until validated. The operational link: use paper-b’s sharp transition criteria and duality to identify the critical locus of the equal-energy point, then compare FK-cluster finite-size scaling with paper-c’s eight-vertex weak-coupling predictions.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
1. Derive the equal-pair-energy condition in \((J,U)\); determine whether it intersects paper-b’s \(J<U\) dual curves or \(J\ge U\) self-dual curve.  
2. Use paper-b’s OSSS finite-criterion to confirm sharpness at candidate points; do not assume criticality.  
3. Simulate the random-cluster/FK representation on \(L=32\)–\(1024\) along the identified transition curve.  
4. Measure wrapping probabilities, largest-cluster fractal dimension, cluster-size distribution exponent, and two-point connectivity; perform finite-size data collapse.  
5. Validate through paper-b’s FK limits (e.g., \(U\to0\) Ising/percolation checks) and dual-curve consistency, then compare exponents with eight-vertex weak-coupling values implied by paper-c.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We propose a conditional test of the Ashkin-Teller equal-pair-energy point’s universality class. Using paper-b’s rigorous random-cluster/FK framework and paper-c’s scaling prediction, we first derive the missing parameter locus, confirm sharpness, then estimate cluster finite-size scaling exponents to test weak-coupling eight-vertex equivalence.

FINAL IDEA: Use rigorous random-cluster/FK and sharp-transition constraints from paper-b to locate the equal-pair-energy Ashkin-Teller point and test paper-c’s predicted eight-vertex weak-coupling scaling via cluster finite-size observables.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-b: Provides a rigorous ferromagnetic phase diagram for the square-lattice Ashkin-Teller model, with sharp transitions via OSSS, duality, and random-cluster (Chayes-Machta / Pfister-Velenik) representations coupled to FK-percolation.
- Paper-c: States that in the special case where two pair energies are equal, Ashkin-Teller critical properties match those of the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit, via a scaling hypothesis.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Paper-b’s random-cluster/FK coupling turns Ashkin-Teller spin transitions into percolation observables. Paper-c’s scaling equivalence predicts a special point on paper-b’s self-dual curve where those observables should match eight-vertex weak-coupling scaling. The integration is operational: use the FK-coupled percolation representation to test and localize the eight-vertex correspondence within the rigorously established phase diagram.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Missing cross-paper knowledge: the exact parameter mapping from the equal-pair-energy Ashkin-Teller point to the eight-vertex weak-coupling limit is not specified in the available abstracts.
- Work on the square-lattice Ashkin-Teller model with ferromagnetic J,U>0, focusing on the self-dual curve J≥U.
- Use paper-b’s random-cluster representation to generate FK-coupled percolation configurations and measure cluster-boundary observables: crossing probabilities, cluster-size moments, and interface fractal dimensions.
- Apply finite-size scaling along the self-dual curve. Hypothesis: cluster-boundary exponents vary continuously, and at the special equal-pair-energy point they coincide with eight-vertex weak-coupling exponents predicted from scaling.
- Validate using paper-b’s duality and known FK-percolation limits, and use sharpness/OSSS bounds to control finite-size corrections.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose using the rigorous random-cluster/FK coupling of the Ashkin-Teller model to test its eight-vertex weak-coupling correspondence. By measuring percolation observables along the self-dual curve, we aim to identify whether the equal-pair-energy point matches eight-vertex scaling predictions, thereby connecting sharp phase-transition proofs with eight-vertex critical phenomena.

FINAL IDEA: Use the Ashkin-Teller random-cluster/FK coupling to test the eight-vertex weak-coupling scaling equivalence at the special equal-pair-energy point through finite-size percolation observables.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
- Paper-b: gives rigorous ferromagnetic square-lattice Ashkin-Teller phase diagram, sharp transitions via OSSS finite-criterion, and a random-cluster/FK representation coupled to FK-percolation.  
- Paper-c: claims, via scaling hypothesis, that the equal-pair-energy Ashkin-Teller case has the same critical properties as the weak-coupling eight-vertex model.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Use paper-b’s random-cluster/FK representation as concrete geometric observables; use paper-c’s scaling claim as a universality target. The mechanism is operational: locate the equal-pair-energy locus in \((J,U)\), generate the associated random-cluster measure, and test whether its finite-size scaling exponents match eight-vertex weak-coupling behavior. Missing cross-paper knowledge: the \((J,U)\) mapping of the equal-pair-energy condition is not given in either abstract.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
1. Derive or numerically locate the equal-pair-energy condition in \((J,U)\) and determine its relation to paper-b’s dual/self-dual transition curves.  
2. Simulate paper-b’s random-cluster representation on \(L=32\)–\(1024\) at that locus.  
3. Measure wrapping probabilities, largest-cluster fractal dimension, cluster-size distribution exponent, and two-point connectivity; estimate finite-size scaling exponents.  
4. Validate criticality using paper-b’s OSSS finite-criterion and sharpness, rather than assuming the point is critical.  
5. Compare exponent estimates with eight-vertex weak-coupling predictions implied by paper-c; if the equal-energy point lies off paper-b’s critical curves, test whether it is a new critical point.

Adopt Researcher A’s finite-size scaling of cluster observables; reject Researcher C’s implicit assumption that the equal-energy point lies on the self-dual curve without derivation; qualify both by adding paper-b’s OSSS sharpness as an independent criticality check.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We test the predicted eight-vertex weak-coupling universality of the Ashkin-Teller equal-pair-energy case by using paper-b’s rigorous random-cluster/FK framework and OSSS finite-criterion. Locating the equal-energy condition and measuring cluster exponents on square lattices would link rigorous phase-transition results to a specific universality class and clarify the scaling hypothesis’s domain.

FINAL IDEA: Use paper-b’s rigorous random-cluster/FK and OSSS phase-transition framework to validate paper-c’s scaling claim that the Ashkin-Teller equal-pair-energy point belongs to the eight-vertex weak-coupling universality class.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We test paper-c’s scaling claim by applying paper-b’s rigorous random-cluster/FK framework and OSSS finite-criterion to the Ashkin-Teller equal-pair-energy point. Deriving the missing parameter mapping and measuring cluster exponents on square lattices would link sharp-transition proofs to a specific eight-vertex weak-coupling universality class and clarify the scaling hypothesis’s domain.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
- Paper-b: For ferromagnetic square-lattice Ashkin-Teller with \(J,U>0\), establishes a complete phase diagram: for \(J<U\), two distinct dual transition curves; for \(J\ge U\), one self-dual transition curve. Proofs use a random-cluster representation, couplings to FK-percolation, OSSS inequality, and a finite-criterion argument.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Paper-b provides a rigorous random-cluster/FK coupling and identifies the self-dual transition locus where Ising and product-spin transitions coincide. Paper-c predicts that a special equal-pair-energy case lies in the eight-vertex weak-coupling universality class. The integration mechanism is to use paper-b’s random-cluster representation to translate paper-c’s scaling claim into testable cluster-geometry observables along the equal-energy/self-dual line.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We propose testing the scaling equivalence claimed in paper-c by applying the rigorous random-cluster and FK-coupling machinery of paper-b to the square-lattice Ashkin-Teller model. If the equal-pair-energy case lies on the self-dual curve, its cluster observables should match weak-coupling eight-vertex critical behavior; paper-b’s sharp phase-transition results would give the first rigorous setting for this universality claim.

FINAL IDEA: Use the rigorous random-cluster/FK phase-transition framework for the Ashkin-Teller model to test the predicted weak-coupling eight-vertex scaling universality on the equal-pair-energy self-dual line.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
- Paper-b: Gives a rigorous ferromagnetic Ashkin-Teller phase diagram; sharp transitions via OSSS, random-cluster/FK representation, and duality.  
- Paper-c: Claims equal-pair-energy critical properties match weak-coupling eight-vertex behavior via scaling.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
I adopt paper-b’s random-cluster/FK representation as the geometric bridge: connectivity observables become testable scaling variables. I adopt paper-c’s scaling hypothesis only as a predicted universality class, not as established equivalence. I qualify both colleagues’ proposals: they assume the equal-pair-energy point lies on the self-dual curve, but this mapping is not in the abstracts and must be derived. Operation: use paper-b’s sharp transition and duality to constrain candidate loci, then use paper-c to predict cluster-exponent values.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
1. Derive the equal-pair-energy condition in \((J,U)\); missing cross-paper knowledge. Do not assume it falls in \(J\ge U\).  
2. For each candidate locus, simulate the random-cluster representation on square lattices \(L=32\)–\(1024\).  
3. Measure cluster observables: largest-cluster fractal dimension, crossing probabilities, cluster-size distribution exponent, and FK limit comparisons.  
4. Finite-size scaling: compare estimates with weak-coupling eight-vertex exponents implied by paper-c.  
5. Validate using paper-b’s finite-criterion/OSSS sharpness: ensure simulations sit on a transition curve and control finite-size corrections.  
6. Use paper-b’s couplings to FK-percolation as consistency checks: known Ising/percolation limits must be recovered.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We propose a conditional test of the Ashkin-Teller equal-pair-energy point’s universality class. Using paper-b’s rigorous random-cluster/FK framework and paper-c’s scaling prediction, we derive the missing parameter mapping, measure cluster finite-size scaling exponents, and compare with weak-coupling eight-vertex predictions, while validating transition sharpness.

FINAL IDEA: Use Ashkin-Teller random-cluster observables and rigorous sharp-transition constraints to test the predicted weak-coupling eight-vertex scaling at the equal-pair-energy point only after deriving its exact parameter locus.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
- Paper-b: rigorous ferromagnetic square-lattice Ashkin-Teller phase diagram; sharp transitions via OSSS finite-criterion; random-cluster (Chayes-Machta / Pfister-Velenik) representation coupled to FK-percolation gives geometric critical observables.  
- Paper-c: scaling hypothesis that the equal-pair-energy case has the same critical properties as the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Adopt paper-b’s random-cluster/FK representation as the concrete observable bridge and its sharpness criterion as a criticality check. Adopt paper-c’s claim only as a predicted universality target. Reject any assumption that the equal-pair-energy point lies on the self-dual curve; its \((J,U)\) locus is missing and must be derived. Operationally: derive the equal-pair-energy condition, place it in paper-b’s phase diagram, and use paper-b’s cluster geometry to test whether finite-size scaling exponents match paper-c’s weak-coupling eight-vertex prediction.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
1. Derive the equal-pair-energy condition in \((J,U)\); determine whether it intersects paper-b’s \(J<U\) dual curves or \(J\ge U\) self-dual curve.  
2. Simulate the random-cluster representation on square lattices \(L=32\)–\(1024\) at that locus; if it lies off a transition curve, test as a potential new critical point rather than assuming criticality.  
3. Measure wrapping probabilities, largest-cluster fractal dimension, cluster-size-moment exponents, and two-point connectivity.  
4. Validate criticality with paper-b’s OSSS/finite-criterion sharpness; use \(U\to0\) Ising FK limit and known percolation behavior as endpoint benchmarks.  
5. Finite-size scaling/data collapse compare estimates with paper-c’s weak-coupling eight-vertex exponents.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We propose deriving the equal-pair-energy locus and testing its critical universality using paper-b’s rigorous random-cluster/FK framework and OSSS sharpness, with paper-c’s scaling claim supplying the eight-vertex weak-coupling exponent target. This connects rigorous Ashkin-Teller phase-transition geometry to a specific universality prediction without presupposing the locus.

FINAL IDEA: Use paper-b’s random-cluster/FK observables and OSSS sharpness to locate the equal-pair-energy Ashkin-Teller point and test its predicted weak-coupling eight-vertex scaling, after deriving its exact \((J,U)\) locus.

papers.text:
Title: Phase Diagram of the Ashkin-Teller Model
Abstract: The Ashkin-Teller model is a pair of interacting Ising models and has two parameters: J is a coupling constant in the Ising models and U describes the strength of the interaction between them. In the ferromagnetic case J,U>0 on the square lattice, we establish a complete phase diagram conjectured in physics in 1970s (by Kadanoff and Wegner, Wu and Lin, Baxter and others): when J<U, the transitions for the Ising spins and their products occur at two distinct curves that are dual to each other; when J\geq U, both transitions occur at the self-dual curve. All transitions are shown to be sharp using the OSSS inequality. We use a finite-criterion argument and continuity to extend the result of Peled and the third author \cite{GlaPel19} from a self-dual point to its neighborhood. Our proofs go through the random-cluster representation of the Ashkin-Teller model introduced by Chayes-Machta and Pfister-Velenik and we rely on couplings to FK-percolation.

Title: On critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model
Abstract: The critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model in the special case where two pair energies are the same are shown to be the same as those of the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit as a consequence of scaling hypothesis.

nodes.text:
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper B: Rigorously establishes the ferromagnetic square-lattice Ashkin-Teller phase diagram for \(J,U>0\), proving sharp transitions via OSSS, a finite-criterion argument, and continuity around the self-dual curve. It provides a random-cluster representation and couplings to FK-percolation.
- Paper C: Argues by scaling hypothesis that, when two pair energies coincide, critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model match those of the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Paper B’s random-cluster/FK representation gives a concrete finite-volume setting for locating the self-dual critical line. Paper C’s scaling equivalence is treated as a hypothesis about the scaling limit of this random-cluster ensemble: along the special equal-pair-energy locus, random-cluster connectivities should exhibit the same universal finite-size scaling as weak-coupling eight-vertex variables. The operational link is duality: B’s self-dual curve is the natural place where C’s two-pair-energy degeneracy should occur. Missing cross-paper knowledge: the exact parameter identification between C’s equal-energy condition and B’s \((J,U)\) self-dual line is not stated.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
1. Use Paper B’s random-cluster representation to simulate finite square lattices on the self-dual curve \(J\ge U\) and near the hypothesized equal-energy point.
2. Measure spin/product-spin susceptibilities, Binder cumulants, correlation lengths, and random-cluster crossing probabilities.
3. Perform finite-size scaling; estimate critical exponents and universal amplitude ratios.
4. Compare with eight-vertex weak-coupling predictions from Paper C. Validation is data collapse with eight-vertex exponent formulas and agreement of amplitude ratios.
5. Mathematically test continuity: check whether B’s finite-criterion and OSSS argument extend scaling covariance from one point to a neighborhood.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project tests whether the rigorously located Ashkin-Teller self-dual critical line from Paper B carries the eight-vertex weak-coupling scaling properties conjectured in Paper C. Using Paper B’s random-cluster representation, we simulate finite systems at the proposed equal-pair-energy point, extract critical exponents and crossing probabilities, and test finite-size scaling against eight-vertex predictions. Success would turn Paper C’s scaling hypothesis into a quantitative, computationally verified statement and provide a route to rigorous universality.

FINAL IDEA: Use the Ashkin-Teller random-cluster/FK representation and rigorous self-dual phase boundaries from Paper B to test and potentially prove the scaling equivalence with the weak-coupling eight-vertex model conjectured in Paper C.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper B: Provides a rigorous ferromagnetic phase diagram, the Chayes-Machta/Pfister-Velenik random-cluster representation, FK-percolation couplings, and OSSS-based sharpness for all transitions. I adopt this as the operational and rigorous framework.
- Paper C: States a scaling-hypothesis equivalence between equal-pair-energy Ashkin-Teller critical properties and weak-coupling eight-vertex behavior. I adopt this only as a conjectural target, not as a proven result; I reject treating scaling equivalence as established.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
The random-cluster/FK representation from Paper B converts Ashkin-Teller spin variables into geometric cluster observables. Paper C’s claim then becomes testable: along the equal-pair-energy locus, FK crossing probabilities, cluster-size moments, and correlation-length exponents should match eight-vertex weak-coupling predictions. The causal link is duality: Paper B’s self-dual vs. dual-curve classification selects whether the equal-pair-energy point has one sharp transition or two; this determines which scaling fields Paper C’s hypothesis must match. I qualify that the exact locus of equal pair energies in Paper B’s \((J,U)\) space is not stated and must be derived from the Boltzmann weights, not assumed to coincide with \(J=U\).

RESEARCH DESIGN:
1. Derive the equal-pair-energy condition in terms of \(J,U\) by equating Ashkin-Teller pair couplings with the symmetric eight-vertex limit; if multiple solutions exist, test each against Paper B’s phase diagram.
2. Simulate finite square lattices using the random-cluster representation exactly on the identified locus.
3. Measure FK wrapping probabilities, cluster-size distribution exponents, spin/product susceptibilities, and Binder cumulants.
4. Perform finite-size scaling and compare exponent estimates and universal amplitude ratios with weak-coupling eight-vertex formulas.
5. Use Paper B’s OSSS sharpness to exclude first-order or off-critical drifts in the scaling window.
Missing cross-paper knowledge: the explicit mapping from equal pair energies to \((J,U)\) must be supplied because the abstracts do not give it.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project tests Paper C’s scaling equivalence as a quantitative hypothesis within Paper B’s rigorous random-cluster framework. By deriving the equal-pair-energy locus from the weights, simulating FK observables there, and comparing finite-size scaling with weak-coupling eight-vertex predictions, the proposal either confirms the conjectured universality or identifies which scaling fields deviate.

FINAL IDEA: Use the random-cluster/FK representation and rigorous phase-diagram constraints from Paper B to derive and test the equal-pair-energy locus where Paper C’s conjectured weak-coupling eight-vertex scaling must hold.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper B: I adopt its rigorous ferromagnetic phase diagram, Chayes-Machta/Pfister-Velenik random-cluster/FK representation, and OSSS sharpness as the operational framework.
- Paper C: I adopt its equal-pair-energy scaling claim only as a conjectural universality target, not as a proven parameter identification.

I reject any assumption that the equal-pair-energy locus is simply \(J=U\) or automatically lies on the self-dual curve; this must be derived from the Boltzmann weights. I qualify both colleagues’ proposals by insisting the missing mapping from equal pair energies to \((J,U)\) and then to eight-vertex weak-coupling weights be made explicit before simulation.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Paper B’s random-cluster/FK representation converts Ashkin-Teller spins into geometric cluster observables. Paper C’s scaling equivalence is then testable on those same observables, with the causal connection being duality: Paper B determines whether the equal-pair-energy point has one sharp transition on the self-dual curve or two transitions on dual curves, which fixes the scaling fields Paper C must match. This is operational because FK crossing probabilities and cluster-size moments are finite-volume observables directly tied to Paper B’s proof.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
1. Derive the equal-pair-energy constraint in \((J,U)\) by equating edge Boltzmann weights in the random-cluster representation; locate its intersection with Paper B’s self-dual/dual curves.

papers.text:
Title: Phase Diagram of the Ashkin-Teller Model
Abstract: The Ashkin-Teller model is a pair of interacting Ising models and has two parameters: J is a coupling constant in the Ising models and U describes the strength of the interaction between them. In the ferromagnetic case J,U>0 on the square lattice, we establish a complete phase diagram conjectured in physics in 1970s (by Kadanoff and Wegner, Wu and Lin, Baxter and others): when J<U, the transitions for the Ising spins and their products occur at two distinct curves that are dual to each other; when J\geq U, both transitions occur at the self-dual curve. All transitions are shown to be sharp using the OSSS inequality. We use a finite-criterion argument and continuity to extend the result of Peled and the third author \cite{GlaPel19} from a self-dual point to its neighborhood. Our proofs go through the random-cluster representation of the Ashkin-Teller model introduced by Chayes-Machta and Pfister-Velenik and we rely on couplings to FK-percolation.

Title: On critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model
Abstract: The critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model in the special case where two pair energies are the same are shown to be the same as those of the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit as a consequence of scaling hypothesis.

papers.text:
Title: Phase Diagram of the Ashkin-Teller Model
Abstract: The Ashkin-Teller model is a pair of interacting Ising models and has two parameters: J is a coupling constant in the Ising models and U describes the strength of the interaction between them. In the ferromagnetic case J,U>0 on the square lattice, we establish a complete phase diagram conjectured in physics in 1970s (by Kadanoff and Wegner, Wu and Lin, Baxter and others): when J<U, the transitions for the Ising spins and their products occur at two distinct curves that are dual to each other; when J\geq U, both transitions occur at the self-dual curve. All transitions are shown to be sharp using the OSSS inequality. We use a finite-criterion argument and continuity to extend the result of Peled and the third author \cite{GlaPel19} from a self-dual point to its neighborhood. Our proofs go through the random-cluster representation of the Ashkin-Teller model introduced by Chayes-Machta and Pfister-Velenik and we rely on couplings to FK-percolation.

Title: On critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model
Abstract: The critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model in the special case where two pair energies are the same are shown to be the same as those of the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit as a consequence of scaling hypothesis.
